title: Telemetry syndication and mesh notes for multi-hop inference
body:
Context and goal:

This doc is a working set of notes for how we standardize and "syndicate" telemetry from the serving runtime through sidecars and into the central observability plane. The focus is multi-hop inference flows (router -> model fanout -> sidecar pooling -> fallback), where metrics and traces currently scatter across tenants and instruments.

Primary objectives:
- Define a compact metric set that is safe to share across tenant, runtime, and model teams (low cardinality baseline + optional high-cardinality probes).
- Establish trace span patterns and annotations for session stitching across multi-model fanout and prefix/KV cache hops.
- Propose dashboard tiling rules so teams can publish derived SLI panels without duplicating raw telemetry or causing query explosion.
- Document pragmatic sampling and syndication rules for exporting traces and metrics to downstream consumers (billing, security, analytics).

Notes / principles (quick):
- Keep core SLI metrics 1:1 (one metric name per semantic meaning). Don't create separate metrics for hosted vs. dedicated unless semantics differ.
- Default telemetry exported to product-facing dashboards must be tenant-aggregated (no per-user PII).
- High-cardinality ownership should be opt-in via feature flags (e.g., heavy prompt-tags, conversation-id tagging).
- Traces should encode a minimal session context: session_id, route, model_variant, kv_warmth, prefix_hit(bool), sampled_reason.

Proposed metric set (compact baseline):
- inference.requests.count — count of accepted requests (tag: route)
- inference.requests.latency_ms.p50/p90/p99 — latency quantiles at request boundary (route, model_family)
- inference.tokens.generated.count — tokens produced per request (route, model_family)
- inference.kv.cache.hit_ratio — ratio (evict vs. hit) (model_variant)
- inference.batching.batch_size.avg — per-queue batch occupancy (pool_id)
- inference.error.rate — errors per 1k requests (error_class)
- inference.fallbacks.count — times a fallback path executed (fallback_type)
- inference.model.load_time_ms — model load latency for cold starts (model_variant)
- inference.cost.token_usd_estimated — estimated cost attribution per token batch (tenant_id optional)

Notes on tags: keep to route, model_family, model_variant (short id), pool_id, region, and a boolean kv_warmth. Avoid tenant_id by default on hosted dashboards; allow tenant-scoped panels in dedicated/enterprise workspaces.

Trace/span pattern (suggested):
- Root span: request:route (attributes: route, route_version, entry_point)
- Child span: router.dispatch (attributes: decision_reason, selected_pool_id)
- Child span: sidecar.encode_request (attributes: prompt_len, prompt_hashish (low bits only))
- Child span(s): model.infer (attributes: model_variant, kv_prefetch:boolean, batch_size)
- Child span: model.kv.load (when kv accessed) -> annotate kv_warmth and kv_latency
- Child span: fallback (if executed) with attributes fallback_type and original_model
- End span: response.serialize (attributes: tokens_out, cost_est)

Annotation conventions:
- session_id: prefer deterministic UUID that persists across retries and fanout. Use sha1(route|tenant|conversation_id) truncated.
- prompt_hash: never log full prompt; store 64-bit hash for correlation only.
- kv_warmth: enum {cold,warm,hot} derived from recent-access-window.
- sampled_reason: one of {always,on-failure,probabilistic,debug} so consumers can reason about distribution.

Sampling and syndication strategy:
- Metrics: full ingestion at 1x for baseline set. Additional high-cardinality metrics go to a lower retention tier and require ticket/flag.
- Traces: mandatory minimal tracing header (trace_id, session_id). Full span export gated by sampling rules:
  - on-failure: always export when inference.error.rate > threshold or response status is 5xx
  - probabilistic: 0.5% global baseline for production traffic, tunable per-pool
  - canary/debug: override via rollout flag with 100% for a given customer or model during experiments
- Syndication: flows for who receives what telemetry
  - billing pipeline consumes tokens.generated and cost metrics; requires tenant_id mapping downstream only in secure context
  - analytics consumes anonymized traces (no prompt text) and aggregated token histograms
  - security/compliance gets trace metadata + a separate audit log (HSM-anchored), not full spans by default

Dashboard tiling and ownership rules (draft):
- Core SLI dashboards: owned by eng-observability. These panels are curated and low-cardinality.
- Model family dashboards: owned by applied-ml. Allowed to create derived panels from core metrics but must reuse core metric names.
- Tenant-specific dashboards: created in dedicated partition with tenant_id tag. Avoid in shared dashboards.
- Panel tiling rules: prefer dashboards that pivot on route or model_family; build tenant drill-down only as a secondary view (card-with-modal).
- Avoid adding both model_variant and tenant_id wide-scan panels in a single dashboard to reduce cardinality blowups.

Example dashboard panel specs (textual):
- Panel A: "Customer-facing latency by route (p90)" — metric: inference.requests.latency_ms.p90, group by route, region. Time-range default 1h, refresh 30s.
- Panel B: "KV warmth distribution" — metric: inference.kv.cache.hit_ratio binned by kv_warmth. Useful for prefetch tuning.
- Panel C: "Batch occupancy heatmap" — metric: inference.batching.batch_size.avg across pool_id and time-of-day. Use downsampled series to limit series count.

Operational run-aways and quotas:
- If a dashboard panel queries > 500 series in one request, recommend converting to cohorted panels or pre-aggregated rollups.
- Query throttling: dashboards should include preflight sampling to detect high-cardinality tag combos and show an inline warning.

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical session_id generation in private deployments where no conversation_id exists (use per-connection monotonic id?). (action: @Ethan Park to prototype)
- How to represent model_quantization_level without exploding cardinality—propose mapping to coarsened bucket names (none, int8, int4, fp16). (action: @Marco Rivera)
- Billing pipeline requires tenant resolution for hosted multi-tenant flow; need secure mapping service to avoid exporting tenant_id to metrics plane (expenses pipeline ticket: JIRA:OBS-4127).
- Sampling budget engine: draft a proposal for a dynamic sampler that increases trace export rate for recently rolled-out model variants. (owner: Claire Gomez)

Attachments / quick refs:
- GH snippet: telemetry exporter config used in prototype (github:repo/telemetry-scripts#34)
- Confluence spec link: confluence:OBS-telemetry-syndication-2026 (working draft for governance)

Quick iteration notes (for next sync):
- Walk through 3 typical incidents and map what metrics/traces would be needed to debug vs current gaps.
- Build a lightweight probe that annotates kv_warmth and emits a compact histogram (buckets: 0-1ms,1-5,5-20,20+).
- Draft example Grafana panels as JSON so infra can add them to the curated dashboard library.

If you touch this doc: add a short note at the bottom with date and what you changed.
